title: Stuffing, Breads, & Potatoes Recipe Roundup
contentHtml:
This is one starchy recipe roundup. Explore all our best recipes for making stuffing, breads, or potatoes this Thanksgiving.

Starches are an essential part of the Turkey Day food pyramid. If you're anything like us here at JKLA World HQ, there will be more than one starch on your plate. Whether that's stuffing, breads and biscuits, or all types of potatoes, we've gathered our essential recipes for you to try below.

Koji-infused stuffing.

Stuffing (or dressing, depending on your persuasion)

Our newest recipe for stuffing follows this year's Warm & Koji theme. This recipe triples down on the filamentous fungus, complete with this homemade koji-fermented butter, a few tablespoons of miso, and a splash of sake to deglaze the pan. Plus, it can easily be made vegetarian by swapping the chicken stock for vegetable stock. Try it for yourself: Sage and Mushroom Stuffing with Koji Butter. 🔗

Sometimes you can't beat the classics. This sage and sausage stuffing is affectionately referred to as a "solid blob of sticky, bready, buttery stuff"—as any good stuffing should be. It's also an easy dish to make ahead and finish off on the big day: Classic Sage and Sausage Stuffing from The Food Lab. 🔗

If you're really thinking outside the box, find a regionally beloved burger joint, take 24 burgers off their hands, and turn it into stuffing. We did it last year, and it worked wonders! If you live in Seattle, head down to Dick's and trying it. And if you're located elsewhere, just make sure you order plain burgers. We're thinking outside the box here; we're not actually trying to have cheese, pickles, ketchup, and iceberg lettuce in our dressing: A Good Dick’s Stuffing. 🔗

Four words: Brown. Butter. Corn. Bread.

Biscuits and Breads

With just two ingredients—self-rising flour and heavy cream—you can have light, airy biscuits with minimal work: 2-Ingredient Cream Biscuits. 🔗

But we'll admit, the above recipe has some plot armor to make the two ingredient shtick work. The self-rising flour works to replace flour, baking powder, and salt, while heavy cream replaces both milk and butter. If you have all those ingredients sitting around (plus some sour cream), a recipe like this might be more your speed anyways: The Food Lab's Buttermilk Biscuits Recipe. 🔗

And for anyone really dedicated to the biscuit game, and willing to put in the work to prove it, these flaky folded biscuits originally published with NYT Cooking are worth their weight in frozen, grated butter: The Secrets to my Flaky Folded Biscuits. 🔗

No-knead breads are the move when you have so many other parts moving in the kitchen. Find the latest incarnation of the recipe on NYT Cooking, or an earlier version over on Serious Eats: Better No-Knead Bread. 🔗

This one has more than two ingredients but only needs four words to justify itself: brown butter corn bread. It also comes together using one one pan! Get the recipe here on Patreon: Brown Butter is the Secret to this Moist and Tender Corn Bread. 🔗

Warm & Koji sweet potato mash.

Golden, Sweet, Mashed, Roasted: It's Potato Time

Potatoes are an essential part of the Thanksgiving table—that's not up to debate. How they're presented, on the other hand, is very much up to debate. If you're looking for a creamy, smooth, super buttery mash, direct your attention to the link to the right: Pommes Purée. 🔗

If you're team light and fluffy mash, you'll want to grab some Russets to ensure they fall apart easily and release minimal starch: Ultra-Fluffy Mashed Potatoes. 🔗

If you like 'em roasted, these extra-crispy potatoes are a science experiment come to life. Parboiling potatoes in alkaline water with baking soda breaks down their exteriors, creating a starchy slurry that crisps up in the oven, enhancing both texture and flavor. They're also easily made gluten-free and vegan, if you opt for oil over butter: The Best Crispy Roast Potatoes Ever. 🔗

If you like your roasted potatoes, well, made of sweet potatoes instead, here's how we would do it: The Easiest Roast Sweet Potatoes. 🔗

If you want your sweet potatoes mashed and infused with koji, this year's recipe is the one for you! Turns out the secret to the densest, sweetest, most flavorful sweet potatoes is just a bit of time: Mashed Sweet Potatoes With Miso Brown Butter. 🔗

Finally, if you like your potatoes in a cheesy hasselback gratin, you wouldn't be alone. This is one of the most popular recipes to ever come out of JKLA World HQ! Get the recipe on NYT Cooking (paywalled), through NYT Cooking's YouTube channel, or for free on Serious Eats: Hasselback Potato Gratin. 🔗
